newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P rates US$1bln Countrywide euro notes A/A-1.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates US$1bln Countrywide euro notes A/A-1.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Standard and Poor's said on Tuesday it had assigned its A/A-1 rating to US$1 billion of euro notes issued by Countrywide Corporation Ltd (CCL).
It said Countrywide's rating outlook was stable.

S&P said the ratings, assigned to Countrywide's short-term and medium-term note programme, were based on the guarantee provided by CCL's parent Countrywide Banking Corporation Ltd (Countrywide), which is based in New Zealand.
Countrywide is rated A/A-1 by S&P, reflecting 100 percent ownership by the Bank of Scotland, rated A+/A-1.
S&P said the ratings also reflected Countrywide's own strong financial profile, its good asset quality, and sound underlying profitability.

S&P said Countrywide, a relatively small retail bank operating in the New Zealand market, had conservative credit policies, which should ensure credit quality was maintained, despite the bank's relatively high growth.

S&P said it anticipated the competitive environment in New Zealand would moderate income and asset growth. However, continuing focus on overhead costs and efficiency of distribution was expected to result in stable profits.
